cls: Immune globulin intravenous (Human), 10% (IVIG); passive immunisation / immunoglobulin replacement
pharm: A purified, polyvalent human IgG preparation (e.g. BIVIGAM) pooled from large numbers of plasma donors, providing a broad spectrum of opsonising and neutralising antibodies for replacement therapy in antibody deficiency
quick: 300-800 mg/kg IV every 3-4 weeks (titrate to IgG trough)
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
No data; benefits of breastfeeding weighed against need
Boxed warning - risk of acute renal failure; minimise dose/rate, ensure hydration, monitor BUN/creatinine
No specific adjustment; hepatic dysfunction reported post-marketing
Renal function, signs of thrombosis, hemolysis, vital signs throughout infusion, IgG trough
summary: Human normal immunoglobulin for intravenous use (IVIG, 10% liquid) is a pooled-plasma IgG product indicated as antibody replacement in primary humoral immunodeficiency in patients 2 years and older. The usual dose is 300-800 mg/kg every 3-4 weeks, individualised to clinical response and IgG trough (target trough at least 500 mg/dL, goal about 600 mg/dL). It carries a BOXED WARNING for thrombosis and for renal dysfunction/acute renal failure; for at-risk patients use the lowest practicable dose and infusion rate and ensure adequate hydration. Adverse reactions, including infusion reactions and aseptic meningitis, are infusion-rate dependent, so infusions begin slowly and are titrated up only if tolerated.
indications: Treatment of primary humoral immunodeficiency (PI) in adults and children 2 years of age and older
Includes the humoral defect of common variable immunodeficiency (CVID)

dosage.c: Adult / child >=2 yr - primary humoral immunodeficiency
dosage.n: Individualise; adjust to maintain IgG trough at least 500 mg/dL (target ~600 mg/dL); from 2nd infusion adjust proportionally to prior trough
Start slow; adverse reaction frequency rises with infusion rate

dosage.d: Increase by 0.8 mg/kg/min up to a maximum of 6 mg/kg/min
dosage.n: Slow or stop for any adverse reaction; resume at a lower comfortable rate if symptoms subside

dosage.c: Patient at risk of renal dysfunction or thrombosis
dosage.n: Boxed warning - ensure adequate hydration before infusion; discontinue if renal function deteriorates

admin: Allow refrigerated product to reach room temperature before use; do not freeze or heat and do not use product that has been frozen or heated
Inspect visually - solution is clear to slightly opalescent, colourless to pale yellow; do not use if cloudy, turbid or containing particulates; DO NOT SHAKE
Do not dilute and do not mix with other IVIG products or other intravenous medications; infuse through a separate dedicated line
Single-use vials - use promptly once entered and discard any unused portion
Ensure the patient is adequately hydrated and not volume-depleted before infusion
Begin at the slow initial rate and titrate upward only if tolerated; monitor vital signs throughout
Slow or stop the infusion if an adverse reaction occurs
moa: Human normal immunoglobulin (IVIG) is replacement therapy that supplies a broad spectrum of neutralising and opsonising IgG antibodies against bacterial and viral pathogens and their toxins, restoring an abnormally low IgG level toward the normal range. The IgG opsonins promote phagocytosis and clearance of pathogens, helping prevent recurrent serious infections in primary humoral immunodeficiency. The full mechanism in PI has not been completely elucidated.

absolute: History of anaphylactic or severe systemic reaction to human immune globulin
IgA-deficient patients with antibodies to IgA and a history of hypersensitivity
relative: Risk factors for thrombosis (advanced age, prolonged immobilisation, hypercoagulable states, prior thrombosis, oestrogen use, indwelling central catheters, hyperviscosity, cardiovascular risk factors)
Pre-existing renal insufficiency or predisposition to acute renal failure (diabetes mellitus, volume depletion, sepsis, paraproteinaemia, age over 65, concomitant nephrotoxic drugs)
Conditions with risk of hyperviscosity (cryoglobulins, marked hypertriglyceridaemia, monoclonal gammopathies)
monitor: Boxed warning - signs and symptoms of thrombosis; assess blood viscosity in patients at risk of hyperviscosity
Boxed warning - renal function (BUN, serum creatinine) and urine output before initial infusion and at intervals; discontinue if renal function deteriorates
Acute severe hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis (have epinephrine immediately available)
Signs of aseptic meningitis, hemolysis and pulmonary (TRALI) reactions

preg: No human data are available to indicate the presence or absence of drug-associated risk and no animal reproduction studies have been conducted. Immune globulins cross the placenta increasingly after 30 weeks of gestation. Use in pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: No human data are available on the presence of the product in breast milk, effects on the breastfed infant or on milk production. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effect on the infant.
renal: Boxed warning: IVIG products have been associated with renal dysfunction, acute renal failure, osmotic nephrosis and death, particularly with sucrose-containing products (this 10% product is sucrose-free). Patients at risk include those with pre-existing renal insufficiency, diabetes mellitus, volume depletion, sepsis, paraproteinaemia, age over 65 or on nephrotoxic drugs. Ensure adequate hydration, use the minimum dose and infusion rate practicable, assess BUN and serum creatinine before the first infusion and at intervals, and consider discontinuing if renal function deteriorates.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is described. Hepatic dysfunction and abdominal pain have been reported during post-marketing use of IVIG products.

major: Live attenuated virus vaccines (measles, mumps, rubella, varicella) - passively transferred antibodies may impair the immune response; defer vaccination and inform the immunising physician of recent therapy
moderate: Do not infuse with or mix with other IVIG products or other intravenous medications in the same line
minor: No other significant pharmacologic interactions described in the label
interactions.diagnostics: Passively transferred antibodies can cause transiently positive serological tests; passive anti-A, anti-B and anti-D may produce a positive direct or indirect antiglobulin (Coombs) test, risking misinterpretation

common: Increased blood pressure, diarrhoea, dizziness, lethargy
serious: Boxed warning - thrombosis (arterial or venous), which may occur even without known risk factors
Boxed warning - acute renal dysfunction / acute renal failure, osmotic nephrosis and death
Severe hypersensitivity / anaphylaxis (greater risk in IgA-deficient patients with anti-IgA antibodies)
Aseptic meningitis syndrome (especially with high doses or rapid infusion)
rare: Hyperproteinaemia, increased serum viscosity, hyponatraemia or pseudohyponatraemia
Theoretical risk of transmissible infectious agents (viruses, CJD agent) from human plasma source
Post-marketing: seizures, vascular collapse, hypotension, pancytopenia/leukopenia, severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome)
emergency: Anaphylaxis - stop infusion immediately and treat with epinephrine and supportive care
Acute thrombotic events (stroke, myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism)
TRALI with severe respiratory distress and hypoxaemia

monitoring: Renal function (BUN, serum creatinine) and urine output before the initial infusion and at appropriate intervals, especially in patients at risk of acute renal failure
Signs and symptoms of thrombosis; baseline blood viscosity in patients at risk for hyperviscosity
Vital signs throughout the infusion; slow or stop for reactions
Signs of hemolysis (direct antiglobulin/Coombs test and haematology if suspected)
Pulmonary status for TRALI; test product and patient for anti-neutrophil antibodies if suspected
Serum IgG trough levels to guide dose adjustment
Serum sodium / serum viscosity in at-risk patients
counsel: Immediately report symptoms suggesting a blood clot - pain or swelling and warmth in an arm or leg, discoloured limb, sudden shortness of breath, chest pain worse on breathing, rapid pulse, or numbness/weakness on one side
Immediately report decreased urine output, sudden weight gain, swelling or shortness of breath, which may signal kidney problems
Report severe headache, neck stiffness, drowsiness, fever, sensitivity to light, painful eye movements, nausea or vomiting (possible aseptic meningitis)
Report tiredness, fast heartbeat, yellowing of skin or eyes, or dark urine (possible breakdown of red blood cells)
Report trouble breathing, chest pain, blue lips/extremities or fever (possible lung reaction)
This product is made from human plasma and carries an extremely low theoretical risk of transmitting infection
Tell your vaccinating provider about recent immunoglobulin therapy as it can interfere with live vaccines such as measles, mumps, rubella and varicella
pk: Immediate IgG availability on infusion (immediate passive antibody)
Median Tmax of total IgG approximately 3.5 hours after infusion
Median terminal half-life of total IgG approximately 30 days (range varies between patients)
Sustained protection over the 3-4 week dosing interval; dose to maintain target trough
Store at 2-8 C for up to 36 months; do not freeze; may be kept up to 4 weeks at <=25 C then use or discard; bring to room temperature before use
pearls: BOXED WARNING: thrombosis can occur with any IVIG product even without recognised risk factors - use the minimum dose and infusion rate practicable and ensure hydration in at-risk patients
BOXED WARNING: renal dysfunction and acute renal failure (more common with sucrose-containing products; this 10% product is sucrose-free) - monitor BUN/creatinine and urine output
Adverse reaction frequency is infusion-rate dependent: start slow (0.5 mg/kg/min for 10 min) and titrate up only if tolerated, max 6 mg/kg/min
Contraindicated in IgA-deficient patients with anti-IgA antibodies and prior hypersensitivity - have epinephrine immediately available
Aseptic meningitis is more likely with high doses (about 2 g/kg) or rapid infusion and usually resolves on discontinuation
Can cause a positive direct/indirect Coombs test and transiently positive serology; defer live vaccines
Dose to an IgG trough of at least 500 mg/dL (target ~600 mg/dL); do not shake the vial and do not dilute or co-infuse with other products
missed: IVIG is administered by a healthcare professional on a scheduled cycle (every 3-4 weeks). If a scheduled infusion is missed, arrange the next infusion as soon as practicable; the dosing interval and dose are adjusted by the prescriber according to IgG trough levels and clinical response. There is no patient-managed missed-dose self-correction.
overdose: Overdose or too-rapid infusion may lead to fluid overload, hyperviscosity, and an increased risk of thrombotic and renal adverse events, particularly in elderly or at-risk patients. Management is supportive with monitoring of haemodynamics, renal function and serum viscosity; slow or stop the infusion if reactions occur.
